text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN

- Federal Minister for Water and Power Nisar Ali Khan told the National Assembly (lower house) that the government had decided to cancel the Keti Bandar thermal power project of Gordon Wu's Consolidated Eelectric Power of Asia by mutual agreement.
- The Pakistan Telecommunication Company Limited (PTCL) has decided to reduce inter-city telephone call charges by 20 percent.
- Five more people fell prey to sectarian violence in Punjab province.
- The government has assigned its "flour coupon" scheme under which 400,000 families living below the poverty line will get monetary assistance to purchase essential commodities.
- A shortfall of 1,000 megawatts of power at the Mangla and Tarbela dames has forced the government to go for loadshedding lasting 10 to 15 days.

- The Clinton administration has expressed its willingness to help Islamabad in the extradition from the United States to Pakistan of Pakistani airforce squadron leader Farooq Khan, who was caught red-handed smuggling heroin.

- Noted human rights activist Aurangzeb Kansi has filed a constitutional petition in the Balochistan High Court against the arrest and handing over of Aimal Kansi to FBI agents by the Pakistan government.
- The government is likely to stop Pakistan Railways from carrying out a major capital expenditure programme worth over 7.0 billion rupees.

- The government may fail to achieve its revenue collection target of 296.4 billion rupees in 1997/98 (July-June), unless some flaws in the proposed amendments in the Income Tax Ordinance through the Finance bill 1997 are removed.
- The Central Board of Revenue has withdrawn regulatory duty on the import of electricity meters.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- The Collectorate of Sales Tax in Lahore has lodged criminal cases against 10 steel re-rolling mills for tax evading to the tune of 4.3 million rupees by misdeclaring and forging official documents.
- Pakistan Railways' rehabilitation and privatisation is expected to be completed within one year.
- The PTCL has increased its local telephone call charges to 1.40 rupees from 1.25 rupees.

- The Corporate Law Authority (CLA) has removed Zafar Moti from his membership of the Karachi and Lahore Stock Exchanges for contravening laws and not handing over the shares and proceeds of shares sold to an investor.
THE NEWS
- Jamaat-i-Islami chief Qazi Hussain Ahmed said he would launch a protest campaign against the government in September.
- The Human Rights Commission of Pakistan has filed a petition in the Balochistan High Court accusing the government of illegally extraditing Mir Aimal Kansi to the United States.
THE NATION
- Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz will pay a two-day visit to the United Sates in the first week of July.
THE MUSLIM
- A spokesman for President Farooq Leghari denied a report that U.S. President Bill Clinton and Secretary of State Madeleine Albright had contacted him over the arrest of Aimal Kansi.
- Jamaat-i-Islami chief Qazi Hussain Ahmed described Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif as a security risk.
- A public rally in Quetta condemned the arrest and extradition of Aimal Kansi to the United States.
- Four people were killed in sectarian violence in three cities of Punjab.
